name: k-LCM (hard version)
description: It is the hard version of the problem. The only difference is that in this version $$$3 \le k \le n$$$. You are given a positive integer $$$n$$$. Find $$$k$$$ positive integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$$$, such that: $$$a_1 + a_2 + \ldots + a_k = n$$$ $$$LCM(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k) \le \frac{n}{2}$$$ Here $$$LCM$$$ is the least common multiple of numbers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$$$. We can show that for given constraints the answer always exists.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ $$$(1 \le t \le 10^4)$$$  — the number of test cases. The only line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$ ($$$3 \le n \le 10^9$$$, $$$3 \le k \le n$$$). It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$k$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case print $$$k$$$ positive integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$$$, for which all conditions are satisfied.
approach_summary: Uncover mathematical invariant or parity constraint. Construct the solution step-by-step maintaining the validity condition without exhaustive search.
